title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Citator. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each image shows all three screens: search results (left), homepage (top right), transcript reader (bottom right). All data is fictional.

options.label: The Citator
options.lineage: Legal research citators: pin cites, star paging, status flags
options.thesis: Every remark is a citable authority: star-paged, flagged, and one click from a perfect cite.
options.viewport: Search results first: fixed date, remark and cite columns, facets on the left, the debated bill's headnote on the right.
options.risk: Could read as a lawyer's tool if the plain-language labels slip; it has to stay easy for occasional users.

raised.raise: Fixed ruled columns: date, remark and cite never move; a corrected, passed or vetoed status restyles the row in place.
One action color, green, reserved for what you can press: copy cite, export, filter, read.
Status is a mark in a fixed cell: filled for done, hollow for pending, a pennant for vetoed or corrected; never a colored badge.
Every cite is a labeled strip with tabular figures: date, session, page, speaker, print number.
One keystroke to the next: J and K jump hit to hit and remark to remark, and the focused remark owns the reader.

options.label: Pleading Paper
options.thesis: The official transcript page, perfected: every quote sits on its real page and line, citable to the line.
options.viewport: Results as slips of the actual transcript page, with hit lines highlighted, the page number top right and a line-level cite below.
options.risk: The most obvious idea for transcripts; monospace text tires long reading and can feel like a court-filing viewer.

options.label: The Bill Line
options.lineage: Midnight transit diagram, New York subway graphics
options.thesis: Every bill rides a line from introduction to the Governor; every remark is a stop on it.
options.viewport: The searched bill's route across the top, with results as stops below, each carrying its line bullet.
options.case: Fuses well, because a NY bill's stages form a literal ordered line staff know by heart; loses on clarity, because quote search and long reading sit awkwardly on a map.
options.risk: The dark enamel tires long reading, and the map serves bills more than transcripts.

options.label: Split-flap Board
options.thesis: Today's floor as a departure board.
options.viewport: Sessions and bills as live rows ranked by time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the record is an archive, not a live feed, and staff don't identify with train stations.
options.kept: Fixed columns that never move while status restyles the row.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Plain-language cards and one bright action color.
options.viewport: One idea per card in a single column, with a bottom bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too casual for official work, and it wastes the density researchers need.
options.kept: One action color reserved strictly for actionable things.
options.risk: Too casual, which you ruled out.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size, with rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides that travels sideways.
options.case: Fuses poorly: slanted containers and sideways travel fight long reading and fast scanning.
options.kept: Status as a mark in a fixed cell: filled, hollow or struck.
options.risk: Mannered and hard to read at length.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: Airline boarding passes and gate boards
options.thesis: Each remark as a segmented pass, on a board that reranks.
options.viewport: Pass segments for date, session, page and speaker, above a ranking board.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the travel framing confuses, and ranking by time doesn't suit relevance search.
options.kept: The citation as labeled segments with tabular figures.
options.risk: A travel costume over legislative content.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One remark owns the screen, and the next is one flick away.
options.viewport: One quote full screen, with an action rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the wrong register for staff, and hostile to research.
options.kept: One keystroke to the next: keyboard jumps between hits and remarks.
options.risk: An entertainment framing, the opposite of the brief.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A government-style legislative research portal, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A navy search band, facets on the left, and blue result titles with snippets.
canonCard.risk: Looks like most government sites, close to the dated-government feel you ruled out.
